Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thank you, operator. Thank you everyone for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. The company's results were released earlier today and are available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on news wire services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call, which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar are Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., Mr. Gener Miao, CMO of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd., Mr. Pan Li, CFO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd., and Mr. Charlie Cao, CFO of JinkoSolar Co., Ltd. Mr. Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business operations and company highlights, followed by Mr. Miao, who will talk about the sales and marketing. Then Mr. Pan Li will go through the financials.
They will all be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the Safe Harbor Provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under the applicable laws. It's now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Li Xiande, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin, and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead, Mr. Li.
We are pleased to announce that thanks to our leading position in N-type TOPCon technology, competitive products, as well as global sales and manufacturing network. Our module shipments grew by 34.1% year-over-year to 23.8GW in Q2, ranking first in the industry. By the end of Q2, we had led the industry as the first solar company in the world to reach a total module shipments of 260GW to nearly 200 countries and regions. This again demonstrated the power of our globalization strategy. In Q2, prices in several segments of the industry chain declined slightly on a sequential basis. We flexibly adjusted our production scheduling strategy and utilization rates for different processes and also optimized our supply chain strategy to control costs.
Gross margin was 11.1% in Q2, almost flat sequentially. Adjusted net income was $52.1 million, slightly down sequentially.
Global demand showed faster growth momentum in the first half of 2024. The newly added installations in China totaled 102GW in the first half, up 30% year-over-year. From January to June, total solar module exports increased by around 20% year-over-year. At the same time, we saw an increase in capacity expansion projects delayed, suspended, or even terminated. As to existing capacity, some manufacturers have cut or suspended production. Coming into Q3, prices in the industry chain were low and volatile, with prices in most segments falling below cash cost. The utilization rates across the industry declined compared to Q2 to an overall low level. We view these irrationally low prices as unsustainable. Meanwhile, government and industry launched control policies to promote the healthy and orderly development of the solar industry.
Financial institutions became more selective, preferring to favor strong and excellent companies with technological innovation and cost control capabilities as well as brand channels advantages. We believe that all these matters will further accelerate the elimination of outdated capacities as well as industrial integration. In the future, we expect companies with robust and sustainable operations to reinforce their industry leadership. The in-depth industrial adjustments are bringing both challenges and opportunities to companies. We will continue to improve our management efficiency, strengthen and expand our globalization advantage, taking on challenges in the industry with our resource advantages and innovative capabilities.
Thanks to our global footprint and the competitiveness of our products. By the end of Q2, the visibility of our order book for 2024 exceeds 80%. We have maintained our overall leading utilization rates in the industry, especially for N-type cells, utilization rates nearly 100%.
We kept refreshing our records for cell efficiencies. At the end of Q2, lab efficiency of our N-type TOPCon-based perovskite tandem solar cell reached 33.24%, a significant leap beyond our previous record of 32.33% last year. The mass-produced efficiency of our 182 TOPCon cells exceeds 26.1%. We firmly believe that TOPCon remains the path with the best economic performance in terms of cost, mass production yield, intellectual property protection, and customer acceptance, and still has room for further cost reduction and efficiency increase. We intend to keep our leading position by gradually adopting new technologies while considering both efficiency improvement and economic return.
We continued to optimize our supply chain to cater to the demands of global clients for low carbon, clean, highly efficient, and reliable products. In Q1 of this year, we unveiled Neo Green panels produced in Zero Carbon Factory as certified by TÜV Rheinland for compliance with the relevant criteria and the requirements. So far, we have received positive feedback from our clients. This once again confirmed our commitment to clean manufacturing and product innovation.
Facing shifts in international trade, continuing expansion of our globalization capabilities is becoming increasingly important. As recently announced, we have entered into a strategic partnership with Renewable Energy Localization Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of PIF, and Vision Industries Company to form a joint venture in Saudi Arabia for the production of 10 GW of high-efficiency solar cells and solar modules. This is another step in our innovative transformation from global sales to global manufacturing and an important milestone for our globalization strategy. With years of experience overseas, we are dedicated to building localized solar ecosystems together with our partners to achieve synergy of resources and complementarity of advantages and further grow our competitiveness in the global market.
We are accelerating the clearing out of P-type capacity to optimize our capacity structure. We expect our annual production capacity for mono wafers, solar cells, and solar modules to reach 120GW, 95GW, and 130GW, respectively, by the end of this year. We expect our advanced capacity structure to continue to lead the industry.
With our advantages in N-type TOPCon technology, competitive products, as well as global sales and manufacturing network, we reiterate our guidance for module shipments to be between 100 and 110 GW for the full year 2024. We will continue to implement our globalization strategy to actively assess market opportunities and mitigate market risks. We expect module shipments to be between 23 to 25 GW for Q3 2024. By the end of this year, we expect mass-produced N-type cell efficiency to reach 26.5%. Overall, we are holding a healthy cash flow. We will continue to optimize the structure of our assets and liabilities, as well as our cash flow levels, strengthening our resistance to risks.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thank you, Ms. Li. Total shipments were 25.3 GW in Q2, with module shipments accounting for approximately 94%. We are pleased that we continue to rank number one in the world for the module shipments as we are increasingly recognized by global clients for our highly efficient and reliable products and services. In terms of geographic mix, approximately 60% of our module shipments went to overseas markets in Q2, with Asia Pacific and Europe accounting for the majority. Sequentially, shipments to the US were relatively stable, and shipments to Europe increased by 40%. Thanks to the continuous improvement in Tiger Neo product strength, Tiger NEO shipments accounted for 85% of total shipments in Q2.
A steady increase from near 80% in Q1 as these modules are increasingly accepted by clients, particularly in China, Europe, and North America. Currently, we lead the industry as the first solar company in the world to reach a cumulative N-type module shipment of 100 GW. They continue to enjoy a premium in global market, with premiums in some markets like Europe, US, and the Middle East, especially high. On the strength of our extensive global sales network, we will continue to optimize our shipments and the product portfolio. We were recognized as the top performer across all reliability categories in the PV Module Reliability Scorecard published by Kiwa PVEL for the 10th consecutive time. We topped the PV Tech 2024 Q2 ModuleTech Bankability Report with the highest triple-A rating.
This is a continuous recognition of our commitment to quality, innovation, and R&D over the long term, as well as clients' longstanding trust in our product quality, bankability, and reliability. Recently, we became one of the few companies to have won both tier one energy storage provider and the tier one PV module manufacturer by Bloomberg. These orders are not only a testament to the power of our outstanding brand, but also an affirmation of our proactive contribution to global energy transformation. As the economics of solar energy become more apparent, we expect demand in the global market to stay around 600GW in 2024 and grow steadily in 2025. In addition to mainstream markets like China, US, and Europe, emerging markets such as Middle East and some countries in Asia Pacific are also showing strong growth potential.
With our accumulated experience in global sales and a growing industry chain footprint, we are confident we will, over time, seize the opportunities brought by the growth in global market demand more rapidly and more highly efficiently, and optimize overseas supply chain to effectively cope with changes in international trade policies. We will continue to optimize our products and services, constantly enhancing our competitiveness globally through strategic market positioning and outstanding client relationship management. With that, I will turn the call over to Pan Li.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar Holding Co. Limited
Thank you, Gener Miao. We're pleased to report sequential growth in module shipments and total revenues in a very challenging Q2. While module prices declined, we reduced costs through supply chain optimization and technology upgrade, improved operating efficiency, optimized asset and liability structure. Gross margin was relatively flat sequentially, and our asset liability ratio was down by one percentage point compared to the year beginning. Despite the challenging situation in the industry, we did not stop returning value to our shareholders for their long-term support. At the beginning of August, we announced a cash dividend of $1.5 per ADS, which was paid today as planned.
In addition, as of today, we have repurchased a total of 5.6 million ADS in an aggregate amount of over $113 million in open market on our share repurchase program announced in July 2022, and in the extended share repurchase program announced in December last year. Let me go into more details now. Total revenue was about $3.3 billion, up 4.4% sequentially and down 21% year-over-year. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to a decrease in average selling price of solar modules. Gross margin was 11.1% compared with 11.9% in the Q1 this year, and a 15.6% in the Q2 last year. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to the decrease in average selling prices of modules.
Total operating expenses were about CNY 525 million, up 24% sequentially and up about 18% year-over-year. The sequential and year-over-year increases were mainly due to the write-off of the net book value of the equipment resulted from the fire accident in Shanxi Province, which was partially offset by estimated insurance proceeds from the fire accident in Q2 this year. Total operating expenses accounted for about 16% of the total revenues in Q2, compared to 13% in Q1, and about 11% in Q2 last year. Net loss attributable to the JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. ordinary shareholders was CNY 13.9 million in Q2 this year.
Excluding the impact of the change in fair value of the convertible senior notes, fair value loss related to the investment in solar supply chain companies, share-based compensation expenses, and net loss resulted from a fire accident in Shanxi. Adjusted net income attributable to the JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. ordinary shareholders was about CNY 52 million. Moving to the balance sheet. At the end of Q2, our cash and cash equivalents were CNY 1.91 billion, compared with CNY 2.4 billion in Q1 this year. AR turnover days were 89 days compared with 100 days in Q1 this year. Inventory turnover days were 82 days compared with 89 days in Q1 this year as a result of improving operating efficiency.
At the end of Q2, total debt was CNY 3.86 billion compared to CNY 3.66 billion in Q1. Net debt was CNY 1.95 billion, compared with CNY 1.22 billion in Q1 this year. This concludes our prepared remarks. We are now happy to take your questions. Operator, please proceed.
Operator
Thank you. If you wish to ask questions, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. If you wish to cancel your request, please press star two. Your first question comes from Philip Shen with ROTH Capital Partners.
Matt Ingram
Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Hi, this is Matt Ingram on for Philip Shen. Thank you for taking our questions. You know, looking into the back half of the year in 2025, how do you see module pricing trending? And then on gross margins, what is it going to take to return to the mid-teens margin levels? And do you think this could be achievable in 2025?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thanks for the question. This is Gener Miao. I think, in general, the market price will stay at a, let's say, a relatively low level for a while for most of the market. It's really because, in general, the oversupply situation is quite obvious across the industry. For sure, the market-wise, it depends on the cost, how fast the cost reduction can catch up with the low price situation right now, right? We at least from what we are seeing right now, quarter by quarter or month by month, the cost reduction is happening almost every day. Hopefully, with the improvement from the cost control and also the, you know, all the actions we are taking or the whole industry is working on, the margin could go back to at least a healthy level as early as possible.
Matt Ingram
Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Okay, great. Thank you. Then kind of on supply and demand, you know, with module prices so low, for so long, is that resulting in any demand elasticity? If so, which countries or regions could we see upside surprise in demand? Then on the supply side, when do you think this oversupply situation across the supply chain gets resolved? Does this happen, you know, next few quarters, next twelve months or longer?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
It's really difficult to forecast, right, which days the market will turn upside down. We see everything is gradually going to that direction, everyone. From the demand side, no matter if US, Europe, or China, or other emerging markets, we still foresee a healthy growth year-over-year. Meanwhile, when we see the supply side, for sure we have seen some newcomers that has dropped their plans to give up what they planned to do previously.
From the policy-wise, we see some China government policy initiative, which is trying to control the new expansion of the capacity, which shows a pretty strong signal to, let's say, constrain the capacity supply side as well. Also the current loss-making market will shake out some of the weak players across the industry too. Adding all those up together, you know, supply side, we see a steady growth year-over-year. The supply side, you know, we see some action taking. It might take some time, but it's moving in the direction to restrict the supply into a more rational level. Adding those two together, we hope give it a several quarters, the things will get back to a rational level. I hope.
Matt Ingram
Analyst, ROTH Capital Partners
Great. Thank you. I'll pass it along.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Alan Lau with Jefferies.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Thank you for taking my question. This is Alan from Jefferies. First of all, the results are actually quite impressive, especially during the backdrop of a very challenging market environment. I got a couple of questions, would like to check with the management. First of all, what is the US shipment amount and also the US shipment expectation in second half of this year? What is your view on the policy risk in the US market, especially there were recently filings of critical circumstances?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
For the US, it's a very special market. We see the market is first for Jinko, we are gradually getting back our market share after the efforts we have taken in the last two years' time. If you look into the total shipment numbers, we have provided the range of 5% to 10% as the annual shipment range. But if we look into Q4, it's roughly 5% to 6%. Seasonally, you know, it will change because, for example, right now there's a rush before the tariffs kick in. Also, as the market demand is kicking up. Seasonally, quarter by quarter, there will be some small changes.
In general, I think it's still falling to the range between 5% and 10% of our total shipment in US. For the long term, we still believe US is a great market because of the demand thanks to the AI drivers. You know, the electricity demand is strong. Also the IRA Act is a strong support to the new capacities both on the manufacturing side and on the utility project development side as well. In long term, we are still a big fan of US solar market. We believe, you know, we will continue to be there to find a, let's say, a stable supply chain to serve our clients in US, even there might be some turbulence on the trade policy side.
We still have some pre-prepared solution on it. Yeah.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
I think you are talking about the urgent, you know, circumstances to the AD/CVD.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Yeah.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yeah. You know, it's really a little bit of risk, but we have proactively managed the situations, and based on the regulations. We think, you know, the risk to Jinko is relatively low.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Is it because of the relatively stable volume from Jinko? Like, there was no spike in volume, so you think it's actually compliant with the rules, right?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
It's a little bit complicated, but you know, we are the mandatory respondent to the case AD/CVD. If you are going to be qualified for the situations, you know, the volume shipments after the filing date of case and the period before, and there should be a significant increase of shipments. We proactively manage the volume. That is one line as I'm saying, you know. There's still some kind of risk, but we think the risk is low for Jinko.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Thank you. It's very clear. And also would like to know what is the progress in Middle East? Because there was a huge announcement on the capacity megawatt in Saudi Arabia. We would like to know what is the estimated timeline of that capacity and what type of policy you expect would be benefited?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
You know, it's really a very strategic move for our international manufacturing. You know, it's not only purely manufacturing facilities in Saudi Arabia, and we are working with the PIF and, you know, Vision Industries. In Saudi Arabia, we have very big ambition for the energy transitions by 2030.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
We work together to localize the productions or advance capacities to give us so the module capacities. Saudi, I think the government has a policy department which is, you know, the goal is to, you know, to help to promote local productions in Saudi Arabia. We expect, you know, after our operational, you know, in 2026, and then the modules in Saudi Arabia locally will be, I think, have a premium compared to, you know, the modules out of Saudi Arabia. On top of that, the government has, you know, has a strong support policies, you know, to the joint ventures in Saudi as well.
Will there be any localization requirement on tendering so that you can ensure all of your modules will be sold, and also even some of your competitors will have to buy your modules because of that localization requirement?
I would like to be more confident, you know, we will have a very unique competitiveness in Saudi and for the Saudi market. Saudi, if you look at the total market size, it's roughly 50 to 60% of the total Middle East. Middle East, we are very optimistic, you know, in the next three to five years. You know, I think you want to expose, you know, detailed policies. There are some policies existing, but it's going to be developed, I think, by the government as well. The current policy is 20% local content with some kind of additional penalty. The big issue is, in Saudi Arabia, there is no any, you know, qualified module producers.
Most of the developers at this stage is they get the waiver letter, you know, by my understanding, because there is no available local, you know, local producers. You know, we, you know, I think we are in a good position to penetrate the markets and, you know, to launch our joint venture.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
You'll be technically the only qualified producers by 2026. That might bring you premium there, right?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
I would love to say that, but I think, you know, we will be the first mover, you know. We take that advantage.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
I see.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
We will be the first mover, yeah.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Then an accounting question on the financials, because I saw in the adjusted calculations of adjusted earnings, actually, it's around RMB 380 million. So is it like RMB 665 million and then you take 58% shareholding on the loss of that, so that you get to RMB 80 million?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
You're talking about EPS or really average?
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
The adjusted net income. It's shown as CNY 378 million. There's a net loss due to the Shanxi fire accident of CNY 380 million. We'd like to know if this CNY 380 million is 58% of CNY 665 million in the A-share level.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yeah, you're talking about, you know, the total numbers for the A-share is kind of, you know, the number you are talking about.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Yeah
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
The US holds 58%. The minority, you know, there's, I think, a separate line, net income attributed to non-controlling interests that consolidated all, you know, the net income should be allocated to the minority interest from the perspective of the US net scope.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Understood. Including the loss from the Shanxi province, right?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yes.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
It's also proportionate.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yes, proportionate.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Yes. Thank you. My final question is, what is the usage of FBR polysilicon now? Can you use 100% of that to save cost?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
You mean the polysilicon out of China, right?
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
The FBR.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Oh, FBR.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Granular polysilicon. Yeah.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yes. I think we, you know, I think we get kind of the, you know, improvement on the utilization levels. Typically it's kind of 30%, you know, to 50%.
Alan Lau
Analyst, Jefferies
Thank you. I'll pass on. Thanks a lot, Charlie.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Thank you.
Operator
Once again, if you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. Your next question comes from William Grippin with UBS.
William Grippin
Director of Equity Research, UBS
Hi. Thanks a lot for the time. Just a couple for me. The first one was on the tandem cell efficiency that you noted in the press release. Could you just talk about kind of where you are in the development process for that technology and how long before you think we could see something become commercially available?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yeah, the tandem is still in R&D stage, but we are optimistic for the, you know, for the future commercialization of the TOPCon plus, you know, the tandem technology. Still, you know, if you look at the time scheme, we believe it's in the next five years, you know, it's still in a laboratory stage. It's possible after the five years it could be commercialized, but it depends a lot on, you know, progress. Back to your question, we don't believe it's commercially 100% visibility at this stage. You know, the earliest time maybe after five years.
William Grippin
Director of Equity Research, UBS
Got it. Thank you. Just on the TOPCon side. Obviously there's been a lot of you know, headlines and reports of litigation, companies claiming IP around TOPCon. A little bit hard to get a good handle on you know, the patent landscape there. Just wondering if you could speak to you know, how comfortable you are with your position sort of in the TOPCon IP landscape across your key markets and maybe any sort of discussions around licensing or you know, other legal actions that maybe you've been having.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
The patents, you know. If you look at, you know, Jinko is kind of the TOPCon promoter, you know, the leader of technology. In addition, three years we invested around 5% to 6% total revenue on R&D, and a significant part we put into the TOPCon. We are really very confident, you know, about our patents, particularly on TOPCon. If you look at the total volume, if you look at the quality, if you look at the, you know, the patterns or, you know, the spread in different countries, particularly out of China. I think at the beginning of this year, we also announced some kind of news. We granted some kind of patents to, one solar company, one solar module companies, one solar cell companies.
That, you know, demonstrate our, you know, strong capabilities on R&D and patent position.
William Grippin
Director of Equity Research, UBS
All right. Thanks very much.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Thank you.
Operator
Your next question comes from Rajiv Chaudhri with Sunsara Capital.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Good morning. I have a few questions. The first couple of questions are just housekeeping. Can you tell us what the depreciation and the CapEx numbers were for Q2 and what the targets are right now for the full year?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Okay. Thank you for the question. In Q2, we reduced our CapEx as compared with Q1, which was the total CapEx in the first half year, about 4 billion RMB. Our prospective total CapEx in the whole year would be adjusted to about 9 billion RMB. Yeah, Rajiv, I think the big question, you know, the big picture is, you know, it's a tough situation right in the industry-wise. But the industry has suffered, I think, in three or four quarters. As TOPCon companies, we carefully manage the companies and, you know, sustainable growth. We balance the shipment for graded and further, you know, solidifying our positions on the cash flows, particularly.
On top of that, we significantly cut the CapEx this year as well as next year, as well as lower the operating expenses and optimize our operations, including the, you know, retrain some labor, you know, labor force. If you look at our CapEx next year, we don't have any plan, you know, CapEx plan except for the Saudi Arabia, you know, capacities, which is a strategic move. Just, you know, for illustration and for your understanding. We think, you know, after several quarters, we cannot, you know, project exactly.
We have seen, you know, the big players, top two, top three, even some kind of relatively middle players have been consolidated or be phased out, you know, during this, you know, the downside, the downward cycle. I think we are getting prepared really to go through the cycle time.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Are you suggesting that CapEx in 2025 will be even less than the CNY 9 billion in 2024?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yes, definitely. Saudi Arabia is very unique even, you know, because we take 40% equity and, really, you know, equity will be $100 million and next year. Except for that, I think we have some kind of maintenance CapEx as well as some kind of investment on R&D, you know, R&D CapEx. Definitely it's going to be, you know, lower next year.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Okay. What about depreciation in the second quarter?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Each month, roughly, you know, if you want to use your financial models, it's kind of CNY 500 million R&D to 600 million R&D you can put in your financial models. Anyway, if you have detailed number questions, you know, I would suggest, you know, you can have a follow-up with, you know, with our IR teams and to give you detailed numbers.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Okay, moving on to the next question, that is on your average selling prices. Your average selling price in Q2 was down quite a bit. It was down actually more than 10%, 15% from Q1. A part of the reason I get from reading the presentation is that DG was 50% of sales, and most of DG is, I think, in China. The combination of focus on China and DG led to more than a pretty sharp decline in ASPs.
Now, as you go into the second half of the year and shipments as a proportion of total shift away from China, shift away from DG, will that provide a more benign backdrop for pricing for you?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
You know, the spot market price, you know, in the last three or six months, is continuing to decline, but we think it's going to be, you know, the lowest level to be stabilized. If you look at financial numbers, because we have different buckets, the utility scale, the DG segment, we have different markets, US, you know, Japan, different regions, and different lead time for signing the contracts. If you look at ASP, and you're right, I think it's reflecting the industry-wide, the downward or slow market price for the modules. We, you know, because we have different lead time, different countries, in each quarter, in a Q2 to Q1, the averages is, you know, downward signs.
We expect a continuing trend in the Q3, but relatively stable in Q4. It's, you know. On our side, if you look at the supply chain perspective, the material costs continue to, you know, decline.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Can we expect that the decline in ASPs will moderate from Q2 to Q3 relative to what we saw in Q1 to Q2?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yes, I would like to say, you know, if you look at Q4 versus Q3, it's gonna be relatively, you know, marginalized.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Can you say that we are at the point where pricing can be expected to be stable or we are not there yet?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
I think, you know, kind of in a time scheme, you know, if you look at the sectors, most of the sectors is suffering, you know, cash losses. We don't believe there's a significant room further. With the base of the capacities, it should be kind of stabilized. If you look at the solar wafer price in a recent week, some of top players, they have increased the spot market price a little bit. Even, you know, poly price has been stabilized. Step by step, I think, you know, you will see the module and as well the solar cell, you know, price.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
I see. Okay. Charlie, your costs were down, you know, apart from the decline in polysilicon prices, your production costs were down quite significantly also in Q2, and that helped you maintain the gross margin at a double-digit level. Can you break down some of the reasons why the costs were down? Can we expect costs to keep on coming down at the same rates that we saw from Q4 to Q1 and then Q1 to Q2? We have had some pretty dramatic declines in costs here, and that is separate from the polysilicon price.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yes. You know, there are a lot of efforts we are working on. You know, continue to optimize our design, you know, and the key materials, the price pressure continues to help improve the working efficiencies and labor costs, you know, cut off and operating expenses, you know, optimizations. There are a lot of efforts we are working on.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Does that mean that gross margin can go up in Q3 relative to Q2?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
No, you know, I don't believe that, you know, frankly. I think, you know, we are confident, you know, that the gross margin will bottom and we try to stabilize.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
But you're not confident that it can go up from Q2 to Q3 yet?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
No, I you know, I would like to say, you know, stabilization is kind of, you know. If you look at our peers, you know, we are in a relatively good position, and stabilization and phase out takes time. I think it's not going to take one or two years, but maybe it take several quarters. On top of that, we you know, we leverage our global manufacturing and the marketing capabilities and optimize the economics.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Okay. Another question is on the N-type market. What do you think the size of the N-type market will be in 2024, this year? I mean, and what will your market share be if you do 90 to 95GW?
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
Rajiv Chaudhri, sorry to interrupt you. We will take this as the final question, and for more questions we can discuss after the call. Is that okay?
Rajiv Chaudhri
Founder and President, Sunsara Capital
Yes.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
Yeah.
Operator
Okay. Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar Company Limited
I think N-type this year is kind of the, you know, the TOPCon dominance. This is a domination year for N-type TOPCon, and the margin and especially for TOPCon roughly at 70 to 75% and Jinko roughly 90%. That's if you look for next year. It should, I think, be 1%, penetration for N-type.
Operator
There are no further questions at this time. That does conclude our conference for today. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

Operator
Hello, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for standing by for JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.'s Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode. After management's prepared remarks, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, today's conference call is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to your host for today's call, Ms. Stella Wang, JinkoSolar's Investor Relations. Please proceed, Stella.
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
Thank you, operator. Thank you everyone for joining us today for JinkoSolar's Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. The company's results were released earlier today and available on the company's IR website at www.jinkosolar.com, as well as on news wire services. We have also provided a supplemental presentation for today's earnings call, which can also be found on the IR website. On the call today from JinkoSolar are Mr. Xiande Li, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited, Mr. Gener Miao, CMO of JinkoSolar Company Limited, Mr. Pan Li, CFO of JinkoSolar Holding Company Limited, and Mr. Charlie Cao, CFO of JinkoSolar Company Limited. Mr. Xiande Li will discuss JinkoSolar's business operations and company highlights, followed by Mr. Gener Miao, who will talk about the sales and the marketing, and then Mr. Pan Li, who will go through the financials.
We will all be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the Safe Harbor Provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. As such, our future results may be materially different from the views expressed today. Further information regarding this and other risks is included in JinkoSolar's public filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. JinkoSolar does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under the applicable law. It's now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Xiande Li, Chairman and CEO of JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. Mr. Li will speak in Mandarin, and I will translate his comments into English. Please go ahead, Mr. Li.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
We are happy to announce that thanks to our advantages of N-type TOPCon technology, competitive products, global marketing and manufacturing layouts, module shipments grew 53.3% year-over-year to nearly 20 GW in Q1, ranking first in the industry. The proportion of N-type shipments increased to nearly 80% in Q1 from approximately 70% in Q4 last year, maintaining our leading position in the industry. Module prices continued to fall in Q1. While the industry average utilization rates declined sharply, we maintained our leading utilization rates at high level. Over 70% of modules were shipped to overseas markets in Q1, while proportion of shipments to Europe and the US significantly increased sequentially. Gross margin was 11.9%, flat sequentially.
Net income was $84.4 million, up 19.8x sequentially. Adjusted net income was $65.1 million, up 1.6% sequentially. Newly added installations in China reached 45.7 GW in Q1, an increase of 35.9% year-over-year. Module exports totaled 61.7 GW, an increase of over 20% year-over-year. The PV industry remains one of the few sectors maintaining a higher growth rate, and we expect the global PV demand to grow approximately 25% to 30% in 2024. Coming into Q2, polysilicon prices continued to decline as supply exceeds demand.
On the other hand, macroeconomic conditions pushed commodity prices higher while increasing market demand drove prices of some materials such as glass and film higher. All those factors combined to keep recent module prices relatively stable at a low level. In the short term, the profitability of integrated solar companies is expected to come under pressure. Yet this distinction in operating capabilities, performance of different companies will have larger difference. We expect that overall production capacity in our industry will shrink with the elimination of weaker players that lack market competitiveness, sustainable production capabilities, and the ability to regularly upgrade and iterate technology. Facing various external challenges, we will focus on enhancing our competitiveness and we are confident to maintain relative advantages compared to our first tier peers.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language] 70%。
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
In Q1, faced with a changing market environment, we flexibly adjusted our sales strategies to better balance shipments and profitability. Leveraging our global footprint and competitive products, our order book visibility for 2024 currently exceeds 70%.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language] TOPCon [Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
With continued pressure along the industrial chain, we continue to deploy new technologies to improve the mass production efficiency of TOPCon cells and module output, while reducing costs through initiatives such as optimization of supply chain, and production process.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
We are also accelerating the clearing out of our P-type capacity. Our N-type capacity is expected to exceed 90% of total capacity by the end of 2024, and we expect our capacity structure to continue to lead the industry.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
As the company with the largest overseas integrated capacity in the industry, we continuously work to expand the global industrial chain. Our 1 GW N-type module capacity in the US has started production, and another 1 GW is expected to start production in Q2 this year. With our advantage of global operation and long accumulated experience in risk management, we are confident to respond to changes in international trade and continue to provide premium products and services to our global clients.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language] IEA [Foreign language] 95% [Foreign language] 2028 [Foreign language]
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
According to the latest predictions by the International Energy Agency, IEA, solar PV and wind will account for 95% of global renewable expansion, benefiting from lower generation costs than both fossil and non-fossil fuel alternatives. By 2028, the share of wind and solar PV in global electricity generation will double to 25%. Solar PV still has enormous growth potential. Meanwhile, declining cost of solar plus storage will continue to improve the economics of investing into PV storage projects and stimulate demand growth for storage projects. We are bullish that solar plus storage will become the major model for future growth in electricity generation, and we are confident to continue to lead the industry with advanced technologies and premium high efficiency products.
Xiande Li
Chairman and CEO, JinkoSolar
[Foreign language] 2024 [Foreign language] 26.5% [Foreign language] 2024[Foreign language] 120 [Foreign language] 110 [Foreign language] 2024 [Foreign language] 24 [Foreign language]26 [Foreign language] 2024 [Foreign language] 100[Foreign language] 110 [Foreign language] 90%。
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
Before turning over to Gener Miao, I would like to go over our guidance for Q2 and the full year of 2024. By the end of 2024, we expect net produced N-type cell efficiency to reach 26.5%. We expect our annual production capacity for mono wafers, solar cells and solar modules to reach 120, 110 and 130 GW respectively by the end of 2024. We expect module shipments to be between 24 to 26 GW for Q2 of 2024, and between 100 and 110 GW for the full year 2024, with N-type modules accounting for nearly 90% of total module shipments.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Thank you, Mr. Li. Total shipments were 21.9 GW in Q1, with module shipments accounting for over 90%, ranking first in the industry again. Under the stressful market prices in Q1, we flexibly adjusted our geographic mix. Over 70% of modules were shipped to overseas markets, especially to Asia Pacific and the emerging markets. Shipments to the US were relatively stable sequentially, while shipments to Europe increased nearly 20%, evidence of further trade reduction. On the demand side, the general trend for global low carbon transformation was unchanged despite problems related to installation and connection in some regions and the quality issues in others. We continue to expect a relatively rapid growth in global demand in 2024.
Our extensive sales network and the deeply rooted local customer service infrastructure will help us to respond to market shifts and adjust flexibly and timely, confidently satisfying customer demand for more reliable, low carbon and compliant PV products. Looking forward to the full year, we expect that the proportion of shipments to Europe and the US to further increase compared to last year. Shipments of competitive high-efficiency N-type Tiger Neo modules accounted for nearly 80% overall. Far exceeding the industry average as the value of Tiger Neo is increasingly recognized by customers. In the European and emerging markets, the Tiger Neo penetration rate exceeds 90%. In terms of segment demand from distribution markets in China, Europe, and Asia Pacific was strong during Q1. Closely following the market trend, we raised the ratio of distribution to approximately 50% in the quarter.
We focus very strongly on building our brand recognition because an outstanding brand is key to gaining the long-term trust of our clients. Recently, we were recognized as a tier one energy storage provider by Bloomberg New Energy Finance due to our outstanding products and the capabilities in energy storage, reflecting our commitment to providing safe and reliable energy storage solutions and the recognition by customers for timely delivery and effective deployment capabilities. Besides, we received the triple A rating once again in the 2024 Q1 release of PV Tech ModuleTech Bankability Report, which demonstrates our leadership in manufacturing activity, reliable quality, market share leadership, sound financial performance, and technology innovation. With that, I will turn the call over to Pan.
Pan Li
CFO, JinkoSolar
Thank you, Gener Miao. We're pleased to report that our solar module shipment increased by about 53% in Q1. Where solar module price declined, we managed to control over costs and expenses. Gross profit margin were flat and adjusted net income slightly improved sequentially. At the same time, thanks to our efforts in debt management, our net debt improved sequentially, leveraging our advantages in N-type technology and global sales and manufacturing network. We're very confident in our growth prospect and will continue to improve the efficiency of our working capital, achieving sustainable growth in operating cash flow and enhance our resilience to risks. Let me go into more details now. Total revenue was CNY 3.2 billion, down sequentially and slightly down year-over-year.
The sequential decrease was mainly attributed to the decrease in the shipments of solar modules, and the year-over-year decreases was mainly attributed to the decreases in average selling price of solar modules. Gross margin was 11.9% compared with 12.5% in Q4 last year. The decreases were mainly due to the decrease in average selling price of modules. Total operating expenses were CNY 426 million, down 18% sequentially. The sequential decrease was mainly due to the decrease in the shipments of solar modules and the lower expense in relation to the settlement of a dispute with one of our customers.
Total operating expenses accounted for 13% of total revenues, compared with 11% in Q4 2023 and 12% in Q1 2023. Net income attributable to JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.'s ordinary shareholders was about CNY 84.4 million, up nearly 20x sequentially. Excluding the impact from a change in fair value of the note, a change in fair value of long-term investments, and the share-based compensation expenses, adjusted net income was about CNY 65 million, slightly up sequentially. Moving to the balance sheet. At the end of Q1 2023, our cash and cash equivalents were CNY 2.44 billion, compared with CNY 2.69 billion in Q4 2023, and slightly improved from CNY 1.48 billion in Q1 2023.
AR turnover days were 100 days compared with 76 days in Q4 and 95 days in Q1 of last year. Inventory turnover days were 89 days compared with 57 days in Q4 and 100 days in Q1 of last year. At the end of Q1, total debt was CNY 3.66 billion compared to CNY 4.38 billion in Q4 of 2023. Net debt was CNY 1.22 billion compared to CNY 1.63 billion in Q4 of 2023. A continuous improvement in our debt structure. This concludes our prepared remarks. We're now happy to take your questions. Operator, please proceed.
Operator
Thank you. If you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. If you wish to cancel your request, please press star and then two. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. Please limit yourself to three questions. The first question comes from Brian Lee. Please go ahead.
Brian Lee
Clean Technology Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Hey, everyone. Thanks for taking the questions. Appreciate it. I know you guys are not in the practice of providing specific margin and ASP guidance anymore, but just given the fluctuations in the pricing environment, can you give us a sense pricing was down, it seems like down to like the low to mid-teens here, ASP per watt if we back out the wafer and the cell revenue in the quarter. Should we expect more ASP degradation in modules embedded in the Q2 guide? And then, what's the margin cadence you expect off the result here in Q1? Should we expect Q2 to be up, down, flat? Maybe H2 views as well if there's more of a recovery there.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Hey, Brian, this is Charlie. Back to your questions. The module price is down in recent three quarters, and that's a fact. We have different regions, different arrangement, long-term versus short-term. If you are talking about Q2, the ASP on average is down a little bit. The most important thing is, we are improving the cost and try our best. At the same time we are adopting the relatively new technology materials. On top of that, we are ramping up. This year our focus is the Shanxi super factories. We're expecting to be fully operational in H2.
For the gross margin and profitabilities, we strongly believe H1 this year, it's reaching the bottom. For quarter by quarter, we expect the gross margin relatively stable for Q2 versus Q1. For H2, we expect more shipments, particularly in the United States as well as in the European markets. On top of that, we are very well in a good position for the Middle East market. It helps the gross margin. That's on. In addition, we know the industry is suffering the very stiff competition, particularly for price.
We are expecting the capacities for the tier two, tier three, and even the capacity which are not able to be technology competitive will be phased out throughout this year. This will help the overall bad supply versus demand situations, particularly in H2.
Brian Lee
Clean Technology Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Okay. That’s helpful. If I summarize, I guess it sounds like ASPs down a little bit more into Q2, and then margin stable in Q2 off the Q1 level. Are you actually seeing quoting activity or what’s the outlook for pricing? I know you said shipment volumes and mix improve in the H2, but how about like for like ASPs? Are you actually seeing? You know, you said 70% of your 2024 is already covered in backlog it sounds like. What’s the pricing dynamic you’re seeing in the H2 versus Q1 and Q2? Are pricing still going down?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Yeah. For the pricing, Brian Lee, we believe it will continue to follow the market, which we believe is already reaching the rock bottom. Compared to the market prices versus the, let's say industry, even the leading cost structures most of the peers or the industry players are under the water right now. That's why we believe the pricing price is reaching the bottom. However, when we look into the improvement of the cost structure-wise, it definitely does not go that fast as the price falls in the last five, six, even eight month time.
That's why the market-wise seem to struggle at the beginning of the year, but we believe once the cost structure start to improve to reach the level of the ASPs and match the level of ASPs, we believe the company or even the whole industry, at least the leading competitive ones, will keep their margin as healthy as possible. Hope that answers your question.
Brian Lee
Clean Technology Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Yes, absolutely. Very helpful. Then maybe last one from me, and I'll jump back in the queue. You also mentioned H2 of the year. It sounds like you're positive on US volume trends growing for you. I know this is pretty fresh. The inception of this AD/CVD potential investigation that was petitioned last week by some of the US suppliers. I know in the fall last year, you guys were deemed to not have been one of the companies dumping or countervailing, and so you weren't subject to any duties. It sounds like this petition is opening that entire case back up potentially. What are your thoughts on the latest trade policy update here given what happened last week?
Do you anticipate any or are you seeing any customer feedback right now that suggests there's more uncertainty for you as you move through the next few quarters? Just kinda how are you navigating it? Thank you.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Well t's still early to see what could be the result of this upcoming AD/CVD petitions. Definitely, from JinkoSolar's perspective, we still prefer a fair trade world, which could benefit not only the JinkoSolar itself, but also the whole industry where we can drive. That's what the whole industry has been doing in the last even two decades. Driving the LCOE of the PV energy more and more competitive, which can help the whole world become greener and more environmentally friendly and less carbon footprint. With trade tariff or the current geopolitical issue, definitely it is a big challenge. It increase a lot of costs.
As a company side, we have no choice but to try our best to adapt to what the market or what the government want. That's why we are working very hard with our lawyers, with our customers, trying to find out the best solution in the US market. Right now, honestly speaking, it's still too early to see what could be the pros and cons for that right now. We might need another, let's say, three, even six months to see what could be the, let's say, upside and downside of this contract. Thank you.
Brian Lee
Clean Technology Analyst, Goldman Sachs
Okay, fair enough. Last one, housekeeping for Charlie. I promise I'll pass it on after this. Charlie, what was D&A in the quarter? What was CapEx in the quarter? And then also, could you tell us what the percent of sales in the US this quarter was and what US ASP range was, dollar per watt or cents per watt in the quarter? Thank you.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
The US shipment roughly 8%. 8% of total Q1 shipments. That's the shipments. The revenue percentage will be higher because the price is dramatically higher, right? If you look at the current market price.
For the total CapEx, we are always assured about. It's last year, we spent roughly CNY 20 billion on the capacity expansion. This year will be 50% lower than CNY 10 billion. Last year, we delivered CNY 25 billion operating cash flow. This year, our target is operating cash flow will be over larger than CNY 10 billion. That's, you know. For Q1, the CapEx is roughly CNY 3 billion and the operating cash was CNY 1.5 billion. Hello?
Operator
Okay. The next question comes from Philip Shen with Roth MKM. Please go ahead.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Hi, everyone. Thank you for taking my questions. First one is a follow-up on Brian's question regarding Southeast Asia, AD/CVD tariffs that could be coming later this year. Was wondering if you could talk about how you plan on managing the retroactive tariff risk. I think you guys talked about increasing your shipments to the US market, or certainly having a high mix to the US through 2024. Can you share how much of your shipment volume in 2024 could go to the US? And then how do you plan on managing that retroactive risk that could be as early as, you know, May or July? Thanks.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Yeah. Firstly, for the number-wise, we still stick to our previous plan that we are not intentionally increase or decrease our shipments to US because of the recent AD/CVD petitions. That's already, you know, within our plan of this year. It is definitely because you know what happened in the last two years in US to Jinko, that's why this year's total shipment numbers or the ratio of the US market definitely will be higher than last year. That's why we're just saying that. For this counter risk or retroactives or the number-wise, we don't have mature solutions right now. That's why we are still, as I just answered Brian's question, we are still talking to the lawyers and the customer to see what could be the best solutions. Right now, at least I'm not aware of any good solutions out there.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Got it. Thank you, Gener Miao. How are your contracts structured? Meaning, oftentimes there's a change of law provision, that may put the risk onto the customer. But does it cover tariffs? Do you have the provisions in all your US contracts so that the risk is on the customer? Or in this case, do you believe that the risk of retroactive tariffs may fall into your camp? Thanks.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
I don't think we can disclose the details of the contract, but definitely customer feel the risk as well. Even there are some language which provide the pass-through risk to the customer end. Definitely the customer side has this, the basic economics of the project financings. If it does, it go beyond certain threshold, then definitely the project will not happen or as planned. That's why we have to go through all those details with our customers, with their lawyers, and even their financing providers to find out the best mutual solution for all parties. It's not that easy to take one case, one solution for all.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. Thank you, Gener Miao. One last question on the US market. What do you think is the amount of channel inventory in the US? We've seen a lot of shipments to the tune of about 5 GW a month, coming to the US over the past year. Do you think there's as much as a year and a half of module inventory in the US, or do you think it's much lower? Can you help us understand what you see? Thanks.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
We have read the notes saying that there's, let's say, oversupply in US market. Even some players, either downstream or upstream, try to get more modules before. That's not AD/CVD, but that's the anti-circumvention. Before anti-circumvention. We read the notes, but from our end we have not been able to verify that directly from the customers or from some of our peers right now. But definitely if we look into the numbers available in the market or some market analyst report, we have seen a massive number of the modules or solar product has been shipped to US. But the grid connection numbers might not support that big number. Definitely we have the same question as you have right now.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. Thanks, Gener Miao. Last question here from me on the fire you guys disclosed over the weekend. Can you talk about the impact Shanxi is supposedly a key part of your margin. You did say that there would be an impact in 2024. Can you quantify in any way? When do you think that facility could come back online? How destructive was the fire? Thanks.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Philip Shen, the impact is still being evaluated. Shanxi super factory, remember, this year we do two phases. Phase I is 14 GW, phase III is 14 GW, another 14 GW. The second phase II, we are stick to the original plan, are expected to start operating in Q3 for the phase II and fully operational in early Q4 this year we are talking about the phase I. Phase I, the fire has an impact on the cell capacity, the 14 GW. We expect the cell capacity will be fully operational by the end of this year. This is our original plan by the end of mid-year.
It's going to have some impact, two quarters roughly, and estimated 3-5 GW. The impact is not significant. It's a very not significant impact for the sales. For the operational side, we have adjust our productions as throughout the global facilities to minimize the impact to our customers. For the cost side and the impact of the operation, we think it's nothing significant. However, for the losses from the fire, we are still evaluating, but the equipment is fully insured by the big insurance companies in China, and we're working on it.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Got it. Thank you very much for the color. I'll pass it on.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Thank you.
Operator
Next question comes from Alan Lau with Jefferies. Please go ahead.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Hello? Hi, sir, can you hear me?
Operator
Hi, Lau. Yes, your line is now w-
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
This is Alan Lau from Jefferies. Thanks management for taking my question. First of all, I would like to ask about a follow-up to the question from Philip Shen on the. Basically, how many or what is the percentage of the contracts you have signed at least have the language that is passing through the potential liability of the delays in AD/CVD? The background of this question is because some of the peers suffered a lot last year when they have procured high-priced polysilicon, and then later on when they failed to deliver the shipment, they even have to pay penalties as per those contracts. I wonder if those language is already there, and it's only a matter of working with your clients to solve the problem. Is there any potential liability in delivering the obligations?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Yeah. Again, I don't think we can disclose that level of detail, but definitely we are case by case working with the customers on this AD/CVD risks, as we always do, right? We got a lot of support from the customers regarding what has happened in the US market in the last two years' time. Definitely we appreciate the support, and we are carrying that love for the future long-term partnership with most of our customers. That's why we never wanna end up with a lose-lose solution. Even if there's a risk, we definitely go ahead with the customer to look into the solutions together. That's why we can maintain our leadership in many markets.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Okay. Understood. The next question is regarding to some of the appears to be one-off income in this quarter. Like the other income actually has surged quarter by quarter. Wonder if that's related to a disposal of our disposal gain in our Xinjiang capacity, and how much of that is related to that?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
In Q1 we have completed the transaction to sell 100% of equity of our Xinjiang facilities. We recognize, I think, roughly, CNY 800 million to 900 million net income impact.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Understood. Also, I recall in the transaction there's further performance, how to say this? It's like a performance guarantee in the next couple of years. Has that fact been factored into this CNY 800 to 900 million or that is completely separated?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
No, we didn't record that performance. The performance obligation or variable considerations from the sale of equity. We did not account on the book. We just recorded the fixed portion for the transaction.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Understood. I think another thing that is quite, I would say, quite impressive compared to a lot of your peers is that you actually do not have any impairment on assets. I wonder if you would think you will have any impairment risk going forward in this year, or because you have a supermajority of your capacities are TOPCon already, so you do not foresee any risk going forward from here?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Yes, you're right. We have very small per capacity, and we accelerated depreciation over five years throughout the last two years. The net book value is not significant.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
That's, yeah, that's impressive. Also, you have mentioned the cash flow in Q1 was actually positive. I wonder if the company has taken initiative to improve the cash flow quarter-over-quarter, because that was one of the concerns of investors as to the operating cash flow.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
The efficiency is still our focus operational efficiencies and minimize the production lead time, logistic delivery time, cash conversion cycles. The Shanxi super factory we are building is one of the key considerations improves the whole cycle conversion and improves the cash flow, minimize the working capitals, the warehouse costs, and the logistic timing.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thanks a lot. Finally, on the buyback, wonder if the company has any guidance on the pace of the buyback, because I've noticed that there's a lot of announcement around that, but wonder if you would provide any guidances on that. Would there be any blackout in buyback after the end of quarter and before the announcement of the results?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Our plan is preliminary plan is the shareholder return is roughly $200 million this year. You can see we release news. We have spent roughly $105 million to repurchase back the ADS. On top of that, which is subject to the board approval, we plan to declare dividends roughly $70 million to $80 million. Together with our plan preliminary plan, this year's shareholder return is roughly $200 million.
Alan Lau
Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Understood. Thanks a lot. I'll pass on.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Welcome.
Operator
Once again, if you have a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. The next question comes from Rajiv Chaudhri with Intrinsic Edge. Please go ahead.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Good morning, and congratulations on a strong performance in a very tough Q1 for the industry. My first question is about the gross margin. It seems like your cost per watt for modules were down roughly 10% from Q4 to Q1. Number one, can you give us an idea of how you were able to achieve such a dramatic decline in cost per watt, given that the polysilicon costs were down as well, but not as significant? Then I have a follow-up on the gross margin as well.
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Yes, a combination of our supply chain and our R&D teams' new technology and improve, lower the consumptions of the materials. We upgraded the TOPCon capacity, adopting the LECO technology and significantly improve our cell efficiencies, while cut a lot of the consumptions of the silver paste. A lot of efforts we are doing that. We have internally a very solid target for the cost reductions. Step by step, we think with quarter by quarter, the cost will be relatively improvement will be relatively quicker. Again, now the industry situation is, module price is drop a lot, but we expect it to be stabilized. Cost takes time, and we will try our best to improve the cost faster.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Charlie, is it fair to think that in the coming quarters, Q2, Q3, and Q4, with all the improvements that you are making, that we can expect costs to improve by 1% to 2% every quarter?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
It depends. Some of things most of things we can control, but some of things were out of control. If you look at the silver the commodity price is up a lot in these months. We're trying to minimize the impact. If you look at quarter by quarter throughout the year, it's definitely the end of this year, the cost will be lower than the cost as of today.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Right. Assuming that the material costs don't change, is the 2% per quarter on a sequential basis a reasonable assumption to make in terms of how you are reducing the costs?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
Yeah. We have internally even bigger targets than the 2% each quarter. If assuming the material cost is the same. Overall cost depending on a lot of things. I think, you know, overall it's going to be improved. Again, we think in the next two quarters, the cost improvement will not be so significant. Because we have done a lot of things, but the commodity price now looks to be kept at a very high level. Considering that, we don't believe the overall cost will be dramatically lower. It's lower, slightly lower in the trend in next two quarters.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Combined with the fact that ASPs, well, that you'll be selling more product in the United States by Q4. It's possible that ASPs are actually up somewhat sequentially from Q3 to Q4. Your costs are coming down by, let's say, even 2%, quarter-over-quarter. It looks like you should be able to get the gross margin to be in the 16%, 17% range by Q4. Is that reasonable?
Charlie Cao
CFO, JinkoSolar
It's difficult to estimate. We think one of the key things with the capacity, some capacity phase out in H2. We think the price will become a relatively rational level. On top of that, we have Shanxi super factory. We have more shipments in the US and some are premium market. It helps our margins even some level of recovery. It depends a lot of things. We think what we are now doing is we do internal things, and we do what we can control.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
I see. Okay. My next question is on market share. Your market share in 2023 was in excess of 15%, closer to 16%, for the year as a whole. In the Q1, it's already in the 17% range. Do you think that as the capacity comes offline as for the rest of the year, that your market share will continue to increase, especially if you hit the 110 GW number for the year?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Well, we never take market share as our, let's say, our target. That's why it's harder to say. Also because of the different definitions, there are different ways to calculate it. It's difficult to really define a, let's say, a fair, well-accepted market share definition. Anyway, we appreciate your calculations on these numbers. Based on my perception, I think it's roughly around 17, 18% of market share where how we are looking at ourselves today. Whether that number could go up or go down, it depends on the competition. It depends on the whole industry. It depends on our peer strategy as well. That's why it's difficult to say that right now.
Definitely, we are doing our best to make sure we deliver the good result from the financial statement-wise. Meanwhile, we are doing our best to serve our customers in the long term, to keep the long-term partnership momentum. Thank you.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Is the market share that you have combined with the brand name that you are developing as well giving you a price premium or an increasing price premium relative to other brands?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Definitely, we believe our brand give us a lot of strength and market acceptance or awareness for sure. Whether it create a market premium, it depends on what numbers you are comparing with. If you compare with nobody in the market, definitely it's the brand itself worth quite a lot. If you compare with the top two or top three, the definition or the acceptance of the customers across the different top brand might not be that much as people imagine. The brand premium in the different market sector in different countries will vary a lot as well.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
I see. A question on the N-type products. What do you think the industry's shipments of N-type products will be in 2024?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Roughly, we believe the market will finish the transition from P-type to N-type by end of this year. Technically it might start from, let's say, roughly 35% to 40% range until year end, 90%, even 95% range. That's what we believe.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
You think the other competitors will also get up to the 90% range by the end of the year?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
I mean the whole industry. Someone might take action faster, someone may be slower. As an industry, we believe that the whole industry will look like.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Now you have been ahead in terms of getting your cost of N-type down, and now your N-type costs are comparable to P-type. What margin premium does that give you over tier two and tier three companies who are behind the cost curve, relative to you guys?
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Let's take this as the last question. Thank you for your question, sir. We believe, if you look into some third-party market intel, for example, there's a, let's say, PV InfoLink. If you compare the P-type, N-type price, the gap is roughly $0.01 per watt peak. If you can roughly calculate how much it will reflect in the margin-wise. It's roughly like 9 to 10% of the margin difference. That's the way we are looking into it.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
I see. Okay.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Thank you.
Rajiv Chaudhri
Portfolio Manager, Intrinsic Edge
Just one last question. Sorry.
Stella Wang
Investor Relations Officer, JinkoSolar
Sorry. Because of the time limit, we need to connect with the next investor. For more questions we can negotiate after the call. Okay. Operator, please connect to the next questions. Hello, operator?
Operator
Okay. The last question comes from Leo Ho, with Daiwa Capital Markets. Please go ahead.
Leo Ho
Equity Research Analyst, Daiwa Capital Markets
Okay. Thanks management. Just a question on the AD/CVD situation. I just wonder for our US capacity, are we using, like, our own solar cell from Southeast Asia? We've been hearing some industry feedback suggesting that probably there may be the cancellation of the wafer-plus-three rules, which means that we cannot use solar cell from Southeast Asia anymore. Do you have any view on that? Thank you.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
I'm not quite sure what policies you are referring to, but based on the Jinko situation, we are fully vertically integrated outside China, that means polysilicon, ingot, wafer, cell, module are now all from non-China sources. That's what we have built in the last two years' time under the US UFLPA. That gives us a lot of advantage and trust in the US market.
Leo Ho
Equity Research Analyst, Daiwa Capital Markets
Okay. Just one more question, if I may. I would like to ask about the EU situation. Aside from, I think publicly announced situation regarding LONGi and also Shanghai Electric, are we hearing any troubles regarding Chinese players exporting to the to Europe? Especially, we've been hearing some weird news suggesting that probably there's one of major module maker with its EU headquarters being raided. I'm not sure if you guys are hearing the same situation. Thank you.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
It's just not something I'm aware of right now. If I have anything, I definitely will let you know.
Leo Ho
Equity Research Analyst, Daiwa Capital Markets
Okay, thanks so much.
Gener Miao
CMO, JinkoSolar
Thank you.
Operator
This concludes the conference call. Please disconnect your lines.
